title: Oppenheimer: first nuclear weapon 'in modern history'

tellings.quote: There's an apocryphal story of a student going up to Oenheimer being like, "You how does it feel to be the first person to create the nuclear weapon?" And he goes, "Uh, I'm the first person in modern history."

a student of his was rumored to come up to him and said, um you know, "You've created the the first atom bomb, you know, how do you feel?" And he said, "I've created the first atom bomb in modern history."
tellings.difference: Adds the link to Vedic death weapons and credits the Bhagavad Gita and the Vedas.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the apocryphal story of Oppenheimer saying he made the first atom bomb 'in modern history'.

as_told.title: Oppenheimer's rumored 'first atom bomb in modern history' remark and Vedic death weapons

plain: J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb in 1945, was supposedly asked by a student how it felt to make the first nuclear weapon, and answered that he was the first "in modern history." Jesse Michels tells this himself on two episodes and calls it apocryphal, a rumor. In one he ties the answer to the Bhagavad Gita and the Vedas, old Hindu scriptures that he says describe weapons of death, which would hint that ancient people knew such weapons.
